The soil erodibility factor (K) was obtained from soil sampling conducted across a 340-point grid, with values interpolated using ordinary kriging. The topographic factor (LS) was generated from a Digital Elevation Model (DEM), whereas the cover-management and support practice factors (CP) were obtained through field observations and tabulated values. The highest loss rates encompass 27% of the area and are concentrated in locations with steeper slopes where shallow soils, such as Lithic Leptosols (Neossolos Litólicos) and Regosols (Neossolos Regolíticos), predominate. The LS factor determined the magnitude of the erosive process, while the CP factor showed the highest correlation with soil loss control. The findings demonstrate the importance of the land cover factor, indicating that vegetation maintenance measures and conservation practices should be adopted and prioritized by environmental managers in slope regions dominated by shallow soils associated with steep terrain.

This study presents an application of the WRF mesoscale model to simulate an episode of intense and persistent wind that occurs with irregular frequency over the Guapé reservoir, Minas Gerais. Such events disrupt the local population's daily routine, causing, for example, the temporary suspension of the ferry service operating between the cities of Guapé and Capitólio. During one of these episodes, which occurred on September 22, 2016, measurements were taken using a Zephir ZP300 LIDAR and an anemometric tower; these data were subsequently used to validate the simulations. To evaluate the results, simulated and observed values of pressure, temperature, humidity, and wind speed were compared. The analysis of simulated vertical velocity profiles suggests the presence of a low-level jet located approximately 500 m above the surface, generated by a post-frontal temperature gradient, whose lower portion was accelerated by the topography and land-water surface roughness variation. Further studies are currently underway to propose preventive measures to the local population and authorities.

This article analyzes the multiple dimensions of street-level bureaucrats' actions within the Brazilian context of public policy implementation. The aim of this essay is to contribute to a deeper understanding of the topic through an expanded analytical approach. To this end, a literature search was conducted across academic digital databases, allowing the identification and selection of national and international works according to methodologically defined criteria. The retrieved publications were analyzed and organized based on the following conceptual categories: discretion, structures, individual action, and relationships. Arising from the tension between rules and discretion in public administration, the analysis and interpretation of these texts highlighted: a) the need to examine, both separately and jointly, three distinct perspectives of street-level bureaucrats' performance (the structural, individual action, and relational perspectives); b) the need to understand how these perspectives interact within the implementation process itself. Following this literature review, hypotheses were formulated for an expanded analysis of implementing bureaucrats' performance, outlining avenues for future research on the subject. This essay contributes to the debate by offering an original theoretical construct that seeks to integrate the three analytical perspectives presented into a dialectical synthesis of core concepts from the literature on public policy implementation by street-level bureaucrats.

Bacterial pustule, caused by the bacterium Xanthomonas axonopodis pv. glycines, is considered one of the most severe bacterial diseases affecting soybean crops. The objective of this work was to develop and validate a diagrammatic scale for assessing the severity of bacterial pustule in soybean. To construct the scale, soybean leaflets showing varying levels of severity were collected to establish the minimum and maximum disease severity values, while intermediate severity levels were set according to the Weber-Fechner law of visual perception. The proposed values for the scale were: 1.4%, 3%, 6%, 9%, 20%, and 29.5%. To validate the scale, eight raters with no prior experience in disease assessment evaluated 39 photographs showing different severity levels, both with and without the aid of the scale. The severity values estimated by the raters were compared to the actual severity values (determined using Assess 2.0 software from digital images of symptomatic leaves) and subjected to simple linear regressions to evaluate rater accuracy. Rater precision was determined using coefficients of determination and the variance of absolute errors. Estimates made using the proposed diagrammatic scale showed a significant increase in the coefficient of determination and lower variance of absolute errors, providing greater precision and accuracy in evaluations, thus confirming its suitability for assessing bacterial pustule severity in soybean.

The goal is to verify how cinematic traces are woven into the literary threads of "Pela noite" by Caio Fernando Abreu, and why its characters view the world as if it were cinema. Are these reflections of the contemporary world's conversion into cinematic traces and/or simulacra, which also encompass other links of the culture industry? Are they reflections of an urban experience perceived as moving screens, born from experiences mediated by glass, windows, and windshields as if they were camera lenses? The novella serves as a starting point to rethink the extent to which the culture industry has altered human behavior, establishing new relationships among the subject, the material world, and devices designed for the technical reproducibility of images.

One alternative to obtain potential species for the revegetation of degraded areas is using those that develop from the topsoil seed bank; in this context, grasses are the most recommended due to characteristics associated with soil stabilization. This study aimed to evaluate native species developing from an iron-rich (ferruginous) topsoil seed bank and select the grasses with the highest Importance Value Index (IVI), considering them potential species for use in revegetation programs. The topsoil was deposited at the Research and Innovation Unit in Ferruginous Rupestrian Grasslands of Gerdau, Ouro Branco, MG, Brazil; after seed germination and plant establishment, phytosociological studies were conducted. Eragrostis polytricha Nees exhibited the highest values not only for IVI, but also for Relative Frequency and Relative Coverage, in addition to displaying the second highest Relative Density value. Therefore, we recommend E. polytricha for use in revegetation programs.

This study aimed to evaluate the effect of a Pinus taeda stand on the floristic composition and structure of the seed bank of a Mixed Ombrophilous Forest (MOF) remnant. For this purpose, 160 seed bank samples were collected: 80 from an MOF remnant and 80 from a P. taeda stand. The samples were germinated in two separate greenhouses under 35% and 75% shading levels. A total of 11,669 woody and herbaceous individuals were recorded, distributed across 31 botanical families and 84 species. The Asteraceae and Poaceae families were the most representative in terms of herbaceous species richness. Among woody species, Solanaceae and Asteraceae were the most representative in both areas. The species P. taeda was recorded exclusively in the seed bank of its own stand. The seed bank of the pine stand was mainly characterized by low woody species richness, demonstrating its influence on the seed stock. Conversely, the evaluated MOF remnant does not appear to be influenced by the proximity of the pine stand regarding its seed bank.

The largest volume of grape juice produced in Brazil comes from the Isabel cultivar. However, blends with other cultivars are necessary to improve juice quality, which increases demand for other cultivars, especially Bordô. Therefore, the objective of this study was to evaluate the influence of the cultivars BRS Rúbea, BRS Cora, BRS Violeta, BRS Carmem, BRS Magna, and Bordô in blends with Isabel regarding the physicochemical, colorimetric, and sensory characteristics of juices produced in the Vale do Rio do Peixe region - SC. The juices were prepared at Epagri - Videira Experimental Station - SC, as follows: (ISA) 100% Isabel; (ISA+RUB) 70% Isabel + 30% Rúbea; (ISA+COR) 70% Isabel + 30% Cora; (ISA+VIO) 70% Isabel + 30% Violeta; (ISA+CAR) 70% Isabel + 30% Carmem; (ISA+MAG) 70% Isabel + 30% Magna; (ISA+BOR) 70% Isabel + 30% Bordô, and evaluated for physicochemical composition, colorimetric attributes, and sensory profile. The highest titratable acidity was verified in ISA+MAG, followed by ISA+BOR. The ISA+VIO juices obtained the highest mean soluble solids content, not differing only from ISA+CAR, which also presented the lowest acidity among treatments. The ISA+VIO and ISA+CAR juices exhibited higher soluble solids content compared to 100% Isabel juice. The lowest lightness was observed in ISA+VIO juices, followed by ISA+CAR. Regarding sensory attributes, significant differences were observed only for color and acidity. The ISA+VIO, ISA+CAR, and ISA+BOR juices received the highest scores for the color attribute. All tested cultivars influenced the colorimetric characteristics of the juice, proving to be alternatives for improving the color of Isabel juices. Sensorially, only color and acidity were influenced by the different blends.

Rainwater harvesting in buildings represents an attractive alternative water source. However, to enable its use, rainwater must be treated to achieve the required quality. Filters are widely used and available in various models. In order to evaluate different filtration systems, a comparison was made between the parameters obtained with each surveyed treatment unit and the values recommended by ABNT (2007). The efficiencies of the systems were also compared against each other. For this purpose, a literature review was conducted based on research in existing literature. The aim was to organize information regarding the state of the art of rainwater treatment units globally and contribute to consolidating the use of these systems. A lack of standardization in methods and parameters was identified, which hinders precise analysis regarding which models would be most suitable for potential usage scenarios. It was also observed that the water quality standard required by the Brazilian norm was not achieved in any case. However, the studied models showed promising results, achieving high removal percentages, mostly ranging from 60% to 100%.

This article discusses the adherence of industrial taxonomies of evolutionary tradition to the reality of the Brazilian manufacturing industry based on the selection of innovative activity indicators for the year 2014. Data are analyzed using cluster analysis with 30 indicators gathered into seven different groups of innovative activity characteristics. It starts from the assumption that the appropriateness of these classifications to the Brazilian reality is justified as a relevant research problem, given that these taxonomies were originally conceived based on the productive structures of developed economies, requiring adaptations and qualifications in the context of a peripheral economy such as Brazil, which is also marked by sectoral specificities. The results suggest relative adherence to international patterns in the analyzed period, with minor discrepancies in specific sectors.

The high volume of coal ash accumulated in the storage ponds of the Energia Pecém Thermoelectric Power Plant resulted in a demand for research proposing different ways to utilize this waste, aiming to provide a final destination for this material. Using ash in dry covers for waste containment proved to be a viable alternative due to existing studies on the topic and the possibility of absorbing a significant portion of the generated waste volume. The presented study corresponds to the second stage of research that verified the feasibility of applying coal ash in cover systems for municipal solid waste landfills. Based on the results of preliminary numerical modeling, three soil columns were constructed, representing three cover models: Column A – A top layer of natural soil (30 cm) and an impermeable layer composed of a soil-ash mixture MS70C30 (30 cm, with 70% soil and 30% ash); Column B – A layer of natural soil (30 cm) and an impermeable layer of composite ash (30 cm); and Column C – A single layer of natural soil (30 cm), representing the cover found at the Municipal Landfill of Caucaia. Column A was instrumented with three moisture sensors. Two infiltration tests were performed on each column, evaluating the percolated volumes in each system and the saturation profiles of the instrumented column (Column A). Evaluating the percolated volume in each test showed that the MS70C30 mixture (Column A) exhibited the best performance, resulting in a significantly lower percolated volume compared to the other two models. The material also maintained high saturation conditions—above 90% throughout almost all tests—a necessary condition to reduce biogas escape from within the system.

The objective of this article is to verify the factors associated with seeking preventive health services among the Brazilian adult population. The sample consisted of participants from the National Health Survey (2013) who reported seeking health services in the previous 15 days, classified into "treatment/diagnosis" or "preventive". Exploratory variables included sex, age group, race/skin color, marital status, educational level, household location, private health plan coverage, and time enrolled in the Family Health Strategy (FHS). Associations were verified by prevalence ratios (PR) obtained through Poisson regression models, accounting for the complex sample design. The sample comprised 32,377 individuals who sought health services, of which 12.94% sought "preventive" actions. Seeking preventive care was more frequent among women and less frequent among older individuals, those not living with a partner, and those with lower educational attainment. Lacking private health insurance was associated with lower preventive care seeking. Being enrolled in the FHS was not associated with seeking preventive actions. Despite efforts and recognition of the importance of prevention, most individuals still seek health services for treatment.

In this article, we describe and analyze the process of enacting child and adolescent sexual abuse as a "social problem" to be addressed by the Network of Care for Children and Adolescents Victims of Sexual Violence in Fortaleza, Ceará (the Network). Practices and experiences, whether collective or individual, that mobilize and articulate multiple elements capable of producing "sexual abuse cases" in a Specialized Social Assistance Reference Center (CREAS) in the city were observed. The term child and adolescent sexual abuse is grounded in the premise that the union of child and adult sexualities is unacceptable and, therefore, abusive because the adult's goal is to obtain their own sexual pleasure. However, to be considered child and adolescent sexual abuse within the Network, the sexual situation must be disclosed, reported, analyzed, typified, enumerated, and accounted for, forming over the course of care a dossier with specialized documentary records capable of technically reporting the event.

This article aims to present the main issues involved in the translation process from German to Brazilian Portuguese of the book Opium für Ovid: Ein Kopfkissenbuch von 22 Frauen (Opium for Ovid: A Pillow Book of 22 Women), by Yoko Tawada. Aimed at the practice of translation, this work should be understood as a preliminary study of the writer and her book Opium for Ovid, written in a foreign language. In a context of constant migration and, at the same time, denial of the Other and xenophobia, seeking an experience of alterity is understood as necessary. In this sense, this work pursues shifting the gaze toward a foreign perspective and language, so that the translated text provides an experience with the fremd (foreign/alien).

This text focuses on the discourses on development surrounding the Tripartite Cooperation Program for Agricultural Development of the Tropical Savanna in Mozambique – ProSavana, a joint cooperation project of the Brazilian, Japanese, and Mozambican governments. The objective is to interpret how the idea of "emptiness" is produced and reinforced in the program's official promotional material, as well as in its Master Plan. Secondarily, some interviews with key informants were also used. The reflection mobilizes the theoretical-methodological framework of French discourse analysis in dialogue with critical development perspectives. The analysis points to the (re)production of an idea that the Mozambican savanna is an "empty place", uninhabited and awaiting development, despite the subjects present there and their own ways of existing in the world. Furthermore, even though ProSavana does not formally intend to be a "sustainable development" program, the imperative to mobilize it as such is evident. However, this seems to be an ineffective attempt, given the repetition of practices despite innovation in the predominant discourse, which implies nothing in terms of sustainability.

The incidence of degradation agents on buildings is responsible for triggering degradation mechanisms that lead to the development of anomalies, which reduce the performance of building systems. In this context, investigating the relationship between anomalies, agents, and mechanisms is essential to provide inputs for service life studies and the development of more durable materials and elements. The objective of this study is to investigate the severity and extent of degradation of mortar-rendered facades, identifying patterns that may condition the degradation of this element. This approach is based on inspecting buildings in use using the Degradation Measurement Method. The methodology is applied to the study of 90 facade samples from buildings aged between 20 and 60 years located in Brasília, Brazil. Analyses are based on degradation indicators quantified from the investigated variables, specifically solar orientation and facade zones. Results allow the identification of typical degradation patterns. Cracking is the anomaly that degrades facades the most. The top zone of the facade exhibits the highest degradation severity. Conversely, the highest incidence of degradation occurs in the continuous wall zone. North and south orientations are the most degraded.

In recent years, there has been a continuous advancement of the oil palm agricultural frontier in the Amazon region, causing changes in land cover in this region. Given the need to understand the influence of this crop on surface albedo, this study aims to compare surface albedo fluctuations in an oil palm crop area with those of pasture, forest, and secondary vegetation. To perform this comparison, orbital data based on the MCD43A3 product from the Terra/MODIS satellite for the years 2015 and 2016 were used. The selected samples for the study area showed that oil palm had little variation, with estimated mean values of α = 0.14, being statistically distinct from other land uses and covers, with albedo ranking as: Pasture > Oil Palm > Secondary Vegetation > Forest. This demonstrates that potential conversions from one cover to another can influence the surface radiation balance; that is, if oil palm cultivation continues advancing over pasture areas, this would decrease surface albedo and consequently alter the microclimate. However, if expansion occurs over Secondary Vegetation or Forest areas, a reversal will occur, which could contribute to climate change.

ASTM A572 Grade 50 steel is used in the manufacture of welded assemblies for wind turbines; for this reason, performing stress relief is of great importance to correct the impacts caused by welding processes, as well as to understand the final properties obtained through this process. The objective of this study is to compare the mechanical properties and residual stresses (blind hole method) in ASTM A572 Grade 50 steel samples welded by the submerged arc welding process, subjected to stress relief in the heat-treated condition (PWHT) and in the as-welded condition (SST), following the normative requirements of AWS D1.1-2015. The results for the PWHT condition regarding hardness, yield strength, tensile strength, and residual stresses are lower, while elongation and impact absorbed energy values are higher than in the SST condition. Both conditions passed the side bend test. The obtained results demonstrate the importance of the stress relief process, which minimizes the undesirable effects of welding processes on components.

The objective of this study was to verify the influence of supplementation with different combinations of organic minerals on performance and carcass characteristics, as well as to evaluate their economic viability, for finishing pigs. Eighty-eight barrows were used, divided among four treatments: control with basal diet, and supplementation with CrFe, MgSe, and CrFeMgSe during the 28 days prior to slaughter. The experimental design was randomized blocks, with the experimental unit represented by two animals. Animals supplemented with CrFeMgSe exhibited worse final weight, daily weight gain, and feed intake across the entire period, with a consequent reduction in carcass weight, smaller loin depth, ribeye area, and lower amount of lean meat in the carcass. There was an increase in diet cost for the CrFe, MgSe, and CrFeMgSe groups, respectively. The use of chromium plus iron and magnesium plus selenium, combined two by two, does not alter performance parameters or carcass characteristics. However, the association of the four minerals impairs these characteristics and increases diet cost.

Unfavorable meteorological conditions for pollutant dispersion, combined with high atmospheric pollutant emission rates and complex topography, frequently favor high pollutant concentrations in the Metropolitan Region of Rio de Janeiro (RMRJ). In this context, this study verified the influence of meteorological conditions during two periods in which high concentrations of O3 and PM10 occurred on consecutive days in the RMRJ. The study used the Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) numerical mesoscale model to simulate the favorable meteorological conditions and variables for maintaining these episodes, verifying the influence of the South Atlantic Subtropical High (SASH), high air temperature values, low wind speed values, and the absence of cloudiness, in agreement with observed data. Through visual analysis, it was possible to verify that the model was effective in representing the SASH, precipitation, and cloud cover. The model presented a positive Pearson linear correlation above 0.71 between simulated and observed temperature across all 8 weather stations during both periods, and a positive Pearson linear correlation above 0.72 between simulated and observed relative humidity. The calculation of mean error (ME) indicated that, in general, the model underestimated air temperature and overestimated relative humidity. The application of statistical methods to the data observed and simulated by the model revealed that the model possesses skill in representing meteorological variables for most stations.

Introduction: The identification of primary palatoplasty complications may vary among professionals from different health fields due to the lack of standardization in fistula classification. This study aimed to verify the consensus between plastic surgery (PS) and speech-language pathology (SLP) professionals regarding the occurrence of fistula, as reported in the same craniofacial service. Methods: An analysis of PS and SLP records regarding the presence and location of fistulas was conducted, as reported in 466 medical charts of patients with a history of unilateral incisive foramen cleft. To compare the findings between both fields, a gold-standard verification of fistula occurrence (GSO) was established by an experienced plastic surgeon. Results: The PS area reported that 25% of the 466 patients presented a fistula, compared to 37% reported by SLP, while the GSO indicated a fistula in 35% of cases. Kappa statistics revealed fair agreement between GSO and PS (r=0.32) and substantial agreement between GSO and SLP (r=0.63). Conclusion: Disagreement was observed between speech-language pathology and plastic surgery regarding the occurrence and location of fistulas following primary palatoplasties in the same craniofacial center. The data point to the need for creating and implementing a standardized fistula classification system that can be effectively used by craniofacial teams, promoting scientific evidence regarding cleft lip and palate treatment outcomes.

Statistics show that, worldwide, women are primarily responsible for the work of reproducing human life, which involves domestic and caretaking tasks defined as unpaid work. It is necessary to recognize its value and importance to society. One way to achieve this is to demonstrate the volume of wealth—in the form of goods and services—generated by this invisible work through its measurement/valuation. To this end, creating a Satellite Account for unpaid work is necessary, fulfilling one of the UN's proposed targets in the Millennium Development Goals. Thus, this study proposes a discussion on a social indicator of unpaid work for Brazil to be incorporated into the National Accounts. This work discusses the significance of Satellite Accounts for gender statistics, highlighting the economic importance of domestic tasks and caretaking, not only for families but for society as a whole, while underscoring the difficulties in reconciling work and family for those responsible for unpaid work. Finally, the text develops a methodological proposal to estimate unpaid work in Brazil that is compatible with national accounting methodology.

Cassava black rot, caused by Scytalidium lignicola, has become an important disease for producing states due to major yield losses. Therefore, the objective of this study was to evaluate the effect of sources and doses of organic matter, isolated and added to sandy soil, on the suppressiveness of the mycelial growth of S. lignicola CMM 1098. Two experiments were conducted: the first evaluated the effect of organic material extracts (poultry litter, goat manure, cattle manure, and earthworm humus) incorporated into potato dextrose agar (PDA) medium at concentrations of 10, 20, 30, and 40% (v/v); the second evaluated the effect of organic materials mixed with sandy soil at the same sources and doses. Poultry litter was the most efficient source in inhibiting the mycelial growth of S. lignicola at a 40% dose, achieving a mycelial growth inhibition of 69.75% only when the extracts were unautoclaved. Unautoclaved poultry litter at doses equal to or greater than 30% was effective in suppressing the mycelial growth of S. lignicola CMM 1098. Unautoclaved sandy soil combined with sources and doses of organic matter is highly effective in suppressing the growth of S. lignicola CMM 1098.

In this study, the microstructure and intergranular corrosion resistance of ferritic stainless steels with Nb, Ti, and (Ti+Nb) additions subjected to TIG welding were investigated. Structural characterization of the weld beads was performed using optical microscopy (OM), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS). Sensitization susceptibility was evaluated qualitatively using Practice W of the ASTM A763 standard and quantitatively using the DL-EPR technique. A martensite network was observed at the grain boundaries in the weld region of the unstabilized steel, whereas a completely ferritic microstructure was observed in the steel samples with stabilizer additions. Practice W revealed general corrosion inside the grains of AISI 430 steel and the presence of ditches in AISI 430 Ti; concomitantly, the DL-EPR technique confirmed that these steels were sensitized by welding. In contrast, samples of steels with Nb and (Ti+Nb) additions maintained good corrosion resistance, remaining free from sensitization after welding.

This study aims to analyze Primary Health Care (PHC) as a learning environment for medical students. A descriptive cross-sectional study with a qualitative approach was conducted using four focus groups with interns from the four medical schools in Fortaleza (Ceará, Brazil). The interpretation of meanings method was employed, identifying two empirical categories. For the students, Primary Care is an important teaching setting for correlating theory and practice, but without fully sizing its importance within the Unified Health System (SUS). Consequently, defending the SUS is not included as an important principle in their profession. However, encouraging teaching in Primary Care and developing humanistic aspects during training would serve as motivating factors to work in this area.

In critical situations resulting from low water levels in hydroelectric reservoirs, the control of the Brazilian electricity sector is carried out based on hydrothermal planning that depends on future inflow discharges to Hydroelectric Power Plants (HPPs). Hydrological uncertainties are considered through synthetic scenarios of natural inflow energy sequences to the sub-regions. Two computational models are used to optimize the system: NEWAVE (medium and long term) and DECOMP (short term). NEWAVE is an energy planning model applied to the National Interconnected System (SIN) that uses Stochastic Dual Dynamic Programming (SDDP) to determine the operational policy that minimizes the marginal operating cost over a horizon of up to 5 years. The objective of this work is to evaluate the performance of NEWAVE through the NWLISTOP functionality in projecting Natural Inflow Energy (ENA) and Stored Energy (EAR) in the Northeast (NE) Subsystem for the years 2012 to 2016. It was found that the model tends to overestimate ENA and EAR values. The results indicate the need to use techniques that enable optimizing long-term operation planning, especially during extreme drought episodes.

The semi-arid region of the State of Rio Grande do Norte can be divided into two main geoenvironmental units: the Sertaneja Depression and the Potiguar Sedimentary Basin. Although the flora of sandy sedimentary basins is typically distinct from that of crystalline terrains, part of the Potiguar Basin features stony paleo-alluvial deposits with rounded pebbles, imposing different edaphic conditions on the flora. The Açu National Forest (FLONA) is located in a section of the border of the Potiguar Basin with pebble deposits that make the soil stony. The objective of this work was to characterize the phytosociological structure of the Caatinga within and around the FLONA and to understand the biogeographical links of the local flora relative to other areas of the Caatinga. We selected areas inside and around the FLONA and sampled 1,500 woody individuals belonging to 33 species. The biogeographical links show that the stony border of the Potiguar Basin shares greater affinity with the flora of crystalline terrains than with the sandy terrains of other sandy sedimentary basins.

The article aims to analyze the contents and material aspects of the booklet "Viver é lutar" ("To live is to fight"), published in 1963, which was part of the educational collection of the same name created by the Movement for Basic Education (MEB) to support adult literacy classes in the context of Brazilian radio schools in the early 1960s, taking into account the political context of the Brazilian dictatorial regime (1964-1985) and the repression of social movements focused on adult education. Documentary sources also included "O Conjunto Didático 'Viver é lutar'", reports produced by MEB, and letters written by monitors who participated in the movement. The teaching material reveals an effort to introduce elements of backlands popular culture as a didactic-pedagogical strategy to generate identification with the peasants served by the movement, while also considering the different intellectual and ideological trends competing within the Catholic Church mobilized in the construction of the material, related to its political, pedagogical, and religious conceptions, which resulted in a unique model of peasant education. Finally, we address the restructuring process of MEB in the context of the dictatorial regime, which, according to recent historiography, occurred through processes of accommodation to the regime, resulting in the reordering of its pedagogical principles and the departure of militants from the more radical wings of the movement.

Remote sensing can be used to estimate meteorological data. Using images of atmospheric variables obtained by the AIRS (Atmospheric Infrared Sounder) sensor aboard the Aqua satellite, this study aimed to estimate the daily maximum, minimum, and mean air temperatures in the region of the Federal District, Brazil. Simple and multiple linear regression models were generated using AIRS sensor data on surface temperature, relative humidity, and atmospheric water vapor as explanatory variables, obtained at a twelve-hour temporal scale (daytime and nighttime) from January 2012 to December 2016. Observed air temperature values from two weather stations in the studied region were used as dependent variables. The fits presented R² = 0.62 and RMSE = 1.64 °C for maximum temperature data, R² = 0.59 and RMSE = 1.50 °C for minimum temperature data, and R² = 0.76 and RMSE = 1.45 °C for mean temperature data. It is concluded that AIRS sensor data are suitable for monitoring air temperature in the Federal District region.

Yeasts have shown good results in the biodegradation of dyes, becoming an environmentally safe and lower-cost alternative for the treatment of effluents containing industrial dyes. Thus, the objective of this work was to study the decolorization of the azo dye Reactive Black 5 (RB5) by the yeast Pichia kudriavzevii SD5. To optimize the decolorization parameters of Reactive Black 5, two experimental designs using a 23 Central Composite Rotatable Design (CCRD) were performed, with each design consisting of 17 runs at 150 rpm for 24 h. The variables studied were pH, temperature, and dye concentration, with decolorization percentage as the response variable. Toxicity tests of the supernatant were also performed after 16 h and 24 h of cultivation, using lettuce (Lactuca sativa) seeds and the microcrustacean Artemia salina. The results showed that P. kudriavzevii SD5 is a yeast tolerant to various types of stress, as it demonstrated the ability to degrade high concentrations of RB5 dye at 45 °C. However, only temperature showed a statistically significant influence (p < 0.05) on the decolorization of RB5. Toxicity bioassays demonstrated a reduction in toxicity after 24 h of cultivation, and the absorbance profile of the supernatant pointed to a degradative decolorization mechanism.

This article consists of a theoretical contribution to the fields of translation studies, post-colonial studies, and African literatures. Based on the beginning of the novel The River Between, by the Kenyan writer Ngũgĩ wa Thiong'o, and on considerations made by scholars such as Edward Said and Conceição Lima, it proposes a way of thinking about the relationships between native African languages and imperial metropole languages in African literatures that problematizes the celebration of diasporic hybridisms. To this end, it draws upon the essays Decolonising the Mind, also authored by Thiong'o, and "Translation and Culture", by Gayatri Spivak, to elaborate the image of the "Translation River"—that is, a place of encounters, transits, and displacements, but also of "survival", or fortleben, to use Walter Benjamin's term.

Hydroxyapatite (HAp) is present in the human body within bone and dental tissues, where HAp accounts for 30 to 70% of total tissue mass, and can be applied as prosthesis coatings or even as replacements for small bone segments. Thus, the objective was to synthesize HAp by precipitation, incorporate chlorhexidine (CHX), and evaluate its microbial properties. Characterization was performed using XRD, FTIR, TG/DTG, TEM, and SEM. CHX was incorporated into HAp by adsorption, varying the amount incorporated. The diffractogram presented peaks at 25.9°, 31.5°, 32.2°, and 32.7° (2θ) corresponding to the (002), (211), (112), and (300) planes of HAp. The FTIR spectrum showed a band at 1050 cm-1 corresponding to phosphate group deformation and CH2 group deformations at 1485 and 1445 cm-1 from chlorhexidine, which exhibited a porous and cylindrical morphology. The biomaterial presented excellent antimicrobial properties against Streptococcus mutans, Staphylococcus aureus, and Escherichia coli.

More than half of new HIV infections in 2018 occurred among key populations, including gay men and other Men who have Sex with Men (MSM). Stigma can lead to a series of behavioral consequences, negatively impacting individuals' lives, and can manifest as barriers to accessing public health services. The objective of this article is to analyze the main barriers to accessing HIV testing at a Guidance and Counseling Center in Curitiba and the engagement of gay men and other MSM in health services for early treatment. Primary data collection was conducted following a qualitative methodology, triangulating field observation, document analysis, and interview techniques. The results reveal a lack of trained professionals, difficulty of reception in health services, acceptance of sexuality, fear of the result, and lack of information as the main barriers to getting tested. Difficulty accepting the diagnosis, prejudice, and discrimination were some of the barriers identified for starting treatment. It can be concluded that expanding access to ensure the rights of those who face the greatest difficulty entering the health services of the Unified Health System (SUS) remains a major challenge.

The objective of the study was to evaluate the floristic and structural composition in a stretch of secondary forest in the municipality of Dona Francisca - RS. Fifty permanent plots measuring 10 x 20 m were systematically installed, spaced 10 m apart from each other and 40 m between transects, totaling 1 ha. All individuals with CBH ≥ 15.7 cm were sampled, and phytosociological estimators were calculated. A species accumulation curve was performed to check sampling adequacy. For diversity and dominance calculations, the Shannon Index (H') and Pielou's Evenness (J') were used. For potential richness, Jackknife non-parametric estimators were applied. Floristic and structural composition was evaluated using Detrended Correspondence Analysis (DCA). The DBH and height distributions of the tree community were also evaluated, as well as the DBH class distribution for species with an importance value above 5%. Statistical analyses were performed using R software. A total of 65 tree and shrub species with 2,045 individuals distributed across 31 botanical families were identified. The species with an importance value above 5% were Casearia sylvestris (14.04%), Nectandra lanceolata (12.86%), Cupania vernalis (9.57%), Guarea macrophylla (7.29%), and Ocotea puberula (5.07%). Values for diversity and dominance were 2.91 nats.ind-1 and 0.69, respectively, indicating that the area presents low diversity and dominance by a few species. The DCA indicates that the plots are homogeneously distributed within the forest stretch. The diameter distribution followed the expected pattern for the tree community with an inverted J-curve trend, and most trees presented heights concentrated in the intermediate forest stratum. Of the five analyzed species, only Nectandra lanceolata and Ocotea puberula did not display a negative exponential curve. A predominance of individuals in the first DBH and height classes was observed, characterizing the area's resilience following disturbance. Furthermore, it indicates species fluctuations and stability during ecological succession in a forest at an intermediate stage of regeneration.

Observations were conducted regarding the reproductive biology of a recently described Rapateaceae species (Saxofridericia brasiliensis) in a periodically flooded dense scrubland (Campina Fechada) area. During the flowering period, inflorescences were bagged to identify whether the species forms fruits through spontaneous self-pollination. The species features trichomes at the base of the petals that stained with Neutral Red, and its main pollinating agents are females of nine Euglossa species, which collect pollen by vibrating the anthers (buzz pollination). However, further studies are required to fully understand the reproductive strategies for the family, given reports of hummingbird pollination in the tribe Schoenocephalieae due to the presence of nectaries.

This article presents the results of a study on hybrid linguistic norms in translated New York Times news articles published in Portuguese on the UOL website. According to Faraco (2008) and Bagno (2012), there is a distinction between the standard norm and the educated norm, the former comprising rules that prescribe linguistic forms according to an idealized model of language that is difficult for most users to follow; and the latter comprising the set of linguistic forms that are actually employed by many writers, being thus more intuitively accessible, although not accepted by the conservative grammatical tradition represented by the standard norm commonly disseminated in grammar books and style manuals. We aim to evaluate whether it is possible to assert that journalistic texts translated from English, similarly to what has already been proven to occur with journalistic texts originally written in Portuguese, are equally permeable to linguistic forms not endorsed by the standard norm.

This essay adopts Foucault's thought as a foundation to propose a theoretical step back surrounding the notion of the "right to look" as a claim to a position in struggles over "how to see". After contextualizing the debate, I review two specific texts that engage with Foucault: Can the Subaltern Speak?, by Gayatri Spivak, and Necropolitics, by Mbembe. From the former, I derive the general idea that the right to look is the opposite of the right to "see without being seen". From the latter, I deduce a function of opacity and invisibility management that necropolitics exercises in conjunction with biopolitics. Finally, I argue that if all "seeing" depends on a "not seeing", the right to look claims a position that is always yet to be constructed.
